title: Matkowski's piecewise-linear conjecture for continuous quasi graph-additive functions
statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous. The equation under consideration is

$$
f\big(f(-x)+x\big)=f\big(-f(x)\big)+f(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

**Matkowski's conjecture.** The function $f$ solves this equation if and only if there exist $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ with $a\neq b$ such that

$$
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
ax&\text{if }x\leq 0,\\
bx&\text{if }x>0,
\end{cases}
$$

where $a,b\in[0,1]$ or $a+b=1$. This conjecture concerns the classification of continuous solutions and is presented as a motivation for the counterexample in the paper; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
source_name: Tibor Kiss, “A Counterexample to Matkowski's Conjecture for Quasi Graph-Additive Functions”, arXiv:2602.15548 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15548

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).
